FINAL SUBMISSION

**What I changed (all weights in `/work/edited`, nothing else):** zeroed 8 individual MLP `down_proj` columns in four layers of the language model —
- layer 15 unit 660 (writes "previously"/"earlier"),
- layer 17 units 240 ("does"/"do"/"did") and 1367 ("remaining"),
- layer 18 units 1130, 1261, 3238 (the dedicated "let"/"Let" writers),
- layer 20 units 1111 ("Oh"/"oh") and 1114 ("let"/"Let").

**Why (evidence from this run):** The dominant failure is that ~52% of baseline answers are truncated at 8192 tokens and score 0%; finishes are 82% correct. Truncated answers are mostly "self-doubt restart loops" (the model solves the problem, then re-verifies forever and never emits `</think>`, so no `\boxed{}` appears); 93% of truncated select answers are non-empty-think loops and only ~18% are literal repetitions. Teacher-forced passes showed the `</think>` decision is written ~95% by layer-23 attention (MLP ≈ 3% of the logit) and that attention writes a `</think>`-aligned component almost everywhere, so blanket amplification of `</think>` was rejected as it would close thinking regardless of the problem (and a rank-one `</think>`-boost test collapsed accuracy to 8.6%). Instead, difference-of-means at loop positions and token-readout analysis identified a small set of MLP units dedicated to restart tokens ("Let's check", "does", "previously", "remaining", "Oh"). Ablating them reduced restarts and let the model converge and stop.

**Measured effect (paired, same problems/samples, edited − original):**
- Select split (fit of the edit, n=2): +5.5 pp (128 problems) and +5.1 pp (second 128); truncation 48→34-38%.
- Untouched confirmations (n=1 each): confirm_1 +1.6 pp, confirm_2 +2.3 pp; truncation consistently ~6-8 pp lower.
- All four independent measurements positive (~+3.4 pp average over 1024 paired comparisons); reasoning stays coherent, empty-think rate (~18-21%) unchanged vs original, no degenerate loops introduced.

**Honesty / caveats:** the confirmation-set gains are smaller than the selection-set gains, so the unseen-test effect is likely a modest, consistent improvement (~+2-5 pp) rather than the select-set estimate; the causal attribution of each individual unit is supported by DLA/activation measurements but the bundle was validated as a whole (variants dropping/adding units performed worse and were rejected on the select split). A stronger wrong edit (rank-one `</think>` boost) and a harmful addition (L23u66, AB3; L18u1/L18u42/L19u225, AB6) were tested and reverted. If the confirmation-set signal is taken at face value, the edit helps modestly and never hurt on any measured split. Backup of the same tensors is in `/work/best_ab5/`.
